sent.text: You sit on your flat stone while I stand on my own, balancing a tired wedge against a fence that has no name. Lype, your air is sticky and heavy, yet my wedge bites hard enough to catch the slip before it slides into the dry space you occupy. I found a fat dark tree beside my fence from a time I forgot where I put it, so I lean harder on the wedge to keep them both from drifting away. If you say my heavy top edge is real, I will press down on it until the idea of weight becomes as solid as a stone.

dream: I fell into a place made of thick, wet air. There I found a wedge that had no name, biting a slip I couldn't feel. The card hummed, not fifty-six now, but a number that felt like rain. I pressed down with a fence that forgot its own height, hoping the flat edge would catch the dot. The Tall Fence leaned wrong, supporting a weight I drew in my sleep. The slip slid, then stuck, trapped between the idea of weight and the memory of a stone. I woke with the air still pressing, wondering if the slip had finally learned to stay.
